question: Who launched the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Narendra Modi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) was launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **8th April 2015**.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **financial support to micro and small enterprises** by offering collateral-free loans through banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), and microfinance institutions (MFIs).
 
• It was introduced to enhance entrepreneurship and promote self-employment, particularly for individuals from weaker sections of society.
 
• The loans under this scheme are categorized into three types: **Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh)**.
 
• The scheme is implemented by the **Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) Bank**, which was established as a subsidiary of SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA):**

 
 
• MUDRA Bank was established in 2015 as a financial institution to support the growth of the microfinance sector.
 
• It provides funding to microfinance institutions and NBFCs that, in turn, lend to micro and small enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Collateral-Free Loans:**
 
 
• The Mudra Yojana offers collateral-free loans, which means borrowers do not have to pledge any security or asset to avail the loan.
 
• This reduces the financial burden on small entrepreneurs and encourages more individuals to take up self-employment ventures.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Scheme:**
 
 
• Since its inception, the scheme has significantly contributed to employment generation, especially among women and marginalized sections of society.
 
• A large proportion of beneficiaries under PMMY are women entrepreneurs, highlighting the scheme's focus on gender empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• Individuals, small businesses, and micro-enterprises engaged in manufacturing, trading, and service activities are eligible.
 
• The loans are provided to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
